summary: Block pooled email-only account adoption and preserve exact browser-session identity and provider logout lineage through tenant switching.
userImpact: Pooled providers cannot adopt an existing shared account by email. Tenant switching requires matching current access and refresh credentials. Invitations cannot initialize a password on an established shared account.
Fresh pooled invitees can enroll through their organization's OIDC, SAML or LDAP provider. Password setup is available only when tenant policy permits it.

Canonical tenant pages load installed plugin entries through tenant-prefixed URLs. Unprefixed pooled pages no longer send an invented default-tenant hint during requests or refresh, and failed refreshes return to the current hostname's login route.

instructions: Review historical provider links and coordinate host/shared-package upgrades. Pooled legacy access/refresh credentials are rejected; arrange an authorized upgrade and reauthentication window, including recovery administrators.

configuration: The provider-level allowVerifiedEmailLinking option must not authorize cross-tenant account linking in pooled mode.

changes: POST /api/auth/switch-tenant requires the refresh cookie to match the exact session of the access principal. Legacy and bearer-only switch calls require a new sign-in.

Invitation acknowledgments support pooled enrollmentMode and policy-dependent requiresPasswordSet. Dedicated onboarding login-method discovery and provider start/login routes require the verified onboarding cookie. Tenant-prefixed invitation and onboarding endpoints enforce invitation/path binding and preserve verified placement context; root compatibility endpoints remain.

GET/HEAD /t/:tenantSlug/_enterpriseglue/plugins/:pluginId/:version/*assetPath serves the same public, digest-verified installed entry bytes as the legacy root route, with no-store caching. Bootstrap entry URL integrity validation is unchanged. Proxies/CDN routing examples must send this alias to the backend, not the SPA.

notes: Uses the existing refresh-token primary key and user revocation version; no schema change. Physical PostgreSQL race checks do not certify all supported database engines.

security: Matching provider email and existing tenant membership are not independent proof of control of a shared user account.
knownLimitations: Combined qualification remains required before release. Package versions are prepared locally; no publication or deployed upgrade is implied.

Single-tenant legacy refreshes retain ID-less access-token compatibility until expiry or explicit revocation. Fresh-invited OIDC/SAML/LDAP browser journeys pass against local emulators; public-edge and customer identity-provider qualification remain pending. Independent account-control enrollment and historical-link disposition remain outstanding.
Plugin assets use the current tenant release assignment, not an immutable page release pin. Only the manifest-declared frontend entry is served; general code-split chunks are not newly supported.
rollback: Do not roll back a qualified identity-isolation fix without reviewing the restored account-linking exposure.
validation: Targeted service, route, middleware, UI, physical PostgreSQL race tests and the integrated OIDC/SAML/LDAP browser-emulator journey pass locally. The existing five-adapter database matrix passes locally with dirty-development evidence, including the Spanner emulator; this is not clean release certification or proof of session races on every adapter. Combined qualification and protected exact-revision CI remain pending.
